tasks.short: Write news reports from checked reporting evidence

steps.what: Choose the news angle and assemble checked event details
Write news story background and event details

loop.purpose: Draft a straightforward news account from checked reporting
loop.input: checked story brief, exact approved quotations and source references
loop.check: Compare each factual assertion, attribution and implied causal link with reporting evidence; quotations must remain exact
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; journalist writes unclear or sensitive sections manually
loop.why_not_simpler: News prose must connect varied facts and context beyond a fixed template

steps.what: Verify the report and hand the final version to the editor

tasks.design: The journalist chooses the angle and checked facts in {DOCS}, then reviews a bounded prose draft. The journalist verifies the exact story before submitting it through {CMS} to the existing editor review and publication process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing must explain the event clearly without losing attribution, background or uncertainty.
tasks.enabler_now: Constrained drafting can express selected reporting, while the journalist retains every factual and editorial decision.
tasks.still_hard: Fairness, sensitive allegations, ambiguous evidence and avoiding invented quotations.
tasks.human_edge: The journalist knows what the reporting establishes and which context changes its meaning.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft prose work; reporting and editorial responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare a source-linked story brief for a broadcast segment
reach.learn: Broadcast format and editorial handoff requirements

evidence.claim: Mediahuis trials first-line news agents with a person publishing; this supports assisted reporting availability, not this task's savings estimate.
The digest reports a suspension following invented AI quotations, supporting exact quotation verification rather than trust in fluent drafts.

assumptions: Boundary is a written news story from completed reporting through editor handoff, excluding fieldwork, separate background research and editor publication. Live broadcast delivery receives no saving from this design.

The journalist produces the story brief in s1: selected angle, checked event facts, dates, source references, exact usable quotations, attribution, caveats and reporting gaps. Selection, capture and confidentiality checks stay fully counted. Missing evidence requires further human reporting, never model completion.

The editor's existing second-person check and publication work remain outside the focal boundary; additional drafting-related editor effort is separately allowed below. No automatic publication is proposed.
Try native templates and style tools before a model step. Sensitive or unsupported material stays in the manual path; existing system runtime earns no labour saving.
research_questions: Does drafting reduce journalist time after source checks and rewriting, without increasing editor corrections?

already_counted.description: Story selection, evidence capture and final verification

incremental.description: Maintain drafting examples and inspect source-reference failures
Additional editor checks of assisted drafts

approvals.approved_version: Exact story text, quotations, evidence references and editor destination; changes void approval; this is submission, not publication

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R86 gives gross14 and net9 after5 focal upkeep;3 extra editor hours are visible. Range0-5% assumes straightforward sourced reports and allows extensive rewriting; no fieldwork, research or broadcast saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather reporting evidence and develop perspectives

steps.what: Gather information through interviews, observation and direct reporting
Develop perspectives and test what the reporting evidence supports

tasks.design: Retain direct reporting and perspective development with the journalist. Existing notes in {DOCS} support scrutiny of evidence and identification of further questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Missing information often requires gaining access, asking questions and observing events.
tasks.enabler_now: No new component is proposed to replace direct reporting or perspective judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Source trust, contradictory accounts and deciding what further reporting is needed.
tasks.human_edge: The journalist notices what is absent, challenges accounts and changes questions as evidence emerges.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in reporting responsibility or time allocation.

evidence.claim: Direct reporting and perspective development depend on source access and contextual judgement; no labour saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is primary reporting and perspective development. The separate background-research task owns archive work; a roll-up must assign overlapping research once.
Sources provide accounts during normal interviews; the journalist produces notes and observations in s1. No new source questionnaire, structured fact flag or automatic truth assessment is introduced.
Use existing reporting and document tools before any custom build. Separate interview arrangement is counted in its own task.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new system or recurring work is proposed.
unknowns: Overlap between archive research and field reporting
research_questions: Which reporting gaps require new interviews rather than faster document processing?

already_counted.description: Primary reporting and contextual perspective development

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross and net0; no interview, observation or perspective time is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Define background research questions and select accessible source collections
Locate background passages and organise their source references

loop.purpose: Locate candidate passages within authorised archive material
loop.input: research questions and retrieved archive documents with document and passage references
loop.output: source-linked candidate background passages and stated gaps
loop.check: Open original passages and compare names, dates, qualifications and context; retrieved agreement is not proof of truth
loop.stop: One retrieval and one narrowed query; use manual search when relevant originals are absent or references fail
loop.why_not_simpler: Use native search first; the bounded reading step helps only when relevant passages use different wording

steps.what: Verify background information against originals and independent evidence

tasks.design: Use native archive search in {OTHER} first, with a bounded answer desk only for locating source-linked passages. The journalist reads originals and verifies claims before recording background notes in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Background facts are spread across documents with different names, wording and dates.
tasks.enabler_now: An archive reading step can offer referenced leads without claiming complete or current knowledge.
tasks.still_hard: Outdated or incorrect archive material and facts that require fresh reporting.
tasks.human_edge: The journalist checks provenance, contradictions and whether the available sources are sufficient.
tasks.altitude: Less passage hunting, with verification and research direction unchanged.

reach.learn: Programme evidence requirements and handoff conventions

evidence.claim: De Volkskrant tests an archive chatbot; that trial supports archive assistance availability rather than complete or accurate background research.
The digest reports significant issues in 45% of more than 3,000 AI-assistant news answers, supporting checks against original evidence rather than assuming fluent answers are reliable.

assumptions: Boundary is background archive and document research, excluding field interviews and story writing. Background work overlapping general reporting must be counted once.

OTHER means the existing editorial archive search system. Archive staff already store document identifiers, dates, text and passage locations during normal publication archiving. No new archive rekeying is assumed; unsupported documents stay in manual search.

The journalist produces questions, relevant entities, date bounds and permitted source collection in s1, with all selection and capture counted. The retrieval step preserves original references and reports missing material; the journalist checks passage meaning in s2 and independent support in s3.
Test native search before adding the bounded reading step. Existing index runtime earns no labour saving; extra archive support is costed below.
research_questions: Does passage assistance reduce total research time after original-source and independent verification?

already_counted.description: Question capture and final background verification
Candidate passage review and manual retrieval corrections

incremental.description: Maintain retrieval checks and inspect failed references
Additional archive access and index support

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R87.75 gives gross12.25 and net6.25 after6 focal upkeep;3 archive support hours are visible. Range0-3% assumes a usable existing archive and allows stale results and manual retrieval; verification remains fully counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange interviews with relevant information sources

steps.what: Choose interview sources and establish a suitable approach
Arrange interviews and agree timing, format and conditions with sources

tasks.design: Keep source selection and interview negotiation with the journalist. Existing communication tools and {CALENDAR} support agreed arrangements without automated source outreach.
tasks.previous_blocker: An interview often needs trust, explanation and negotiation before scheduling is possible.
tasks.enabler_now: No new component is proposed without evidence of a separable repeated scheduling burden.
tasks.still_hard: Reaching a source, negotiating conditions and protecting confidential arrangements.
tasks.human_edge: The journalist understands why a source may hesitate and can explain the purpose and boundaries.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in source relationships or interview authority.

reach.task: Arrange an informed contributor handoff for a segment

evidence.claim: Interview arrangements depend on access and source negotiation; no labour reduction is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is source choice and interview arrangement, excluding the interview itself and separate reporting.

Sources provide availability and conditions in response to contact during s2, after the approach is chosen. The journalist records agreed details in existing tools; no pre-existing availability feed or new source form is assumed.
Use native calendar functions before custom scheduling. Existing calendar runtime is not labour.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new component or ongoing process is added.
unknowns: Share of interviews needing unusual conditions
research_questions: Are scheduling delays caused by calendar entry or by source access and negotiation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross and net0; source access and negotiated arrangements remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Less constrained draft composition and archive passage hunting, with reporting and source decisions retained.
reach: Prepare source-linked story and background briefs for producers
role.ambitious_version: A journalist who can explain both the evidence behind a story and what remains unverified.
